```{r setup, include=FALSE}

library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
library(gtExtras)
library(sf)
library(tmap)
library(glue)

tmap_mode("view")
```

```{r read-data}
# Pinned copies of the 14d-r2 forecast snapshot from the election-modeling
# repository (data/forecast/2026): per-race posterior summaries, the target
# race list with candidates, incumbency and PVI, and OCPF receipts frozen at the
# 2026-10-20 cutoff.
races <- read_csv("forecast_14d_r2_races.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
targets <- read_csv("forecast_14d_r2_target.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
finance <- read_csv("forecast_14d_r2_finance.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
# 75% predictive intervals (12.5th and 87.5th percentiles of each race's draws),
# derived from the same snapshot by _make_intervals.py.
intervals <- read_csv("forecast_14d_r2_intervals.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

party_abbrev <- c(
    "Democratic" = "D",
    "Republican" = "R",
    "Unenrolled" = "U",
    "Independent" = "I",
    "Workers Party" = "WP",
    "Gulf War Veteran" = "GWV"
)

pvi_string <- function(pvi_n) {
    case_when(
        pvi_n <= -0.5 ~ str_c("R+", round(abs(pvi_n))),
        pvi_n >= 0.5 ~ str_c("D+", round(pvi_n)),
        TRUE ~ "EVEN"
    )
}

#' Margin labeled with the favored side's party, so a race against an
#' unenrolled opponent reads "U+12" rather than "R+12".
margin_string <- function(margin, opp_pty) {
    case_when(
        margin <= -0.5 ~ str_c(opp_pty, "+", round(abs(margin))),
        margin >= 0.5 ~ str_c("D+", round(margin)),
        TRUE ~ "EVEN"
    )
}

cand_label <- function(name, pty, town, incumbent) {
    str_glue("{name} ({pty}-{town}){if_else(incumbent, '*', '')}")
}

receipts <- finance |>
    select(target_id, role, receipts) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = role,
                values_from = receipts,
                names_prefix = "receipts_")

contested <- targets |>
    select(target_id,
           office,
           district,
           district_display,
           dem_candidate_name,
           dem_candidate_municipality,
           dem_candidate_incumbent,
           comparison_candidate_name,
           comparison_candidate_party,
           comparison_candidate_municipality,
           comparison_candidate_incumbent,
           incumbent_status,
           PVI_N) |>
    left_join(races |>
                  select(target_id,
                         dem_margin = point_margin,
                         dem_win_prob = dem_win_probability),
              by = "target_id") |>
    left_join(intervals |>
                  select(target_id,
                         margin_low = lower_75,
                         margin_high = upper_75),
              by = "target_id") |>
    left_join(receipts, by = "target_id") |>
    mutate(chamber = if_else(office == "State Senate", "Senate", "House"),
           # The Senate shapefile spells out "and"; one target uses "&".
           district = str_replace(district, " & ", " and "),
           PVI = pvi_string(PVI_N),
           # District pages on mapoli.us, e.g. state-rep/third-barnstable.html
           district_url = str_c(
               "https://mapoli.us/districts/",
               if_else(chamber == "Senate", "state-senate/", "state-rep/"),
               str_replace_all(str_to_lower(district), "[^a-z0-9]+", "-"),
               ".html"),
           opp_pty = party_abbrev[comparison_candidate_party],
           model = margin_string(dem_margin, opp_pty),
           Incumbent = case_when(
               incumbent_status == "Dem_Incumbent" ~ "Dem",
               incumbent_status == "GOP_Incumbent" ~ "GOP",
               TRUE ~ ""),
           Democrat = cand_label(dem_candidate_name,
                                 "D",
                                 dem_candidate_municipality,
                                 dem_candidate_incumbent),
           Opponent = cand_label(comparison_candidate_name,
                                 opp_pty,
                                 comparison_candidate_municipality,
                                 comparison_candidate_incumbent))
```

```{r map-setup}
house_geom <- read_sf("../../_gis/HOUSE2021/HOUSE2021_POLY.shp") |>
    st_make_valid() |>
    st_simplify(dTolerance = 100, preserveTopology = TRUE) |>
    select(district_display = REP_DIST) |>
    inner_join(contested |> filter(chamber == "House"),
               by = "district_display")

senate_geom <- read_sf("../../_gis/SENATE2021/SENATE2021_POLY.shp") |>
    st_make_valid() |>
    st_simplify(dTolerance = 100, preserveTopology = TRUE) |>
    select(district = SEN_DIST) |>
    inner_join(contested |> filter(chamber == "Senate"),
               by = "district")

stopifnot(nrow(house_geom) == sum(contested$chamber == "House"),
          nrow(senate_geom) == sum(contested$chamber == "Senate"))

margin_palette <- c("#FF4949", "white", "#0F4392")

race_popup_vars <- c(
    "PVI" = "PVI",
    "Democrat" = "Democrat",
    "Opponent" = "Opponent",
    "Dem win" = "dem_win_prob",
    "Model margin" = "model",
    "Dem receipts" = "receipts_dem",
    "Opponent receipts" = "receipts_opp"
)

race_popup_format <- list(
    dem_win_prob = tm_label_format(fun = function(x) scales::percent(x, 1)),
    receipts_dem = tm_label_format(fun = scales::dollar),
    receipts_opp = tm_label_format(fun = scales::dollar)
)

race_layer <- function(geom, group, show_legend = TRUE) {
    tm_shape(geom) +
        tm_polygons(
            fill = "dem_margin",
            fill.scale = tm_scale_continuous(
                values = margin_palette,
                limits = c(-40, 40),
                midpoint = 0,
                outliers.trunc = c(TRUE, TRUE),
                ticks = c(-40, -20, 0, 20, 40),
                labels = c("R+40", "R+20", "EVEN", "D+20", "D+40")
            ),
            fill.legend = if (show_legend) {
                tm_legend(title = "Model margin")
            } else {
                tm_legend_hide()
            },
            fill_alpha = 0.7,
            col = "black",
            lwd = 1,
            id = "district_display",
            popup.vars = race_popup_vars,
            popup.format = race_popup_format,
            group = group
        )
}
```

Incumbency provides a big advantage in legislative elections. Our
[Massachusetts legislative model](https://bwbensonjr.github.io/election-modeling/)
shows a 9-point lift for incumbent Democrats and a 16-point lift for
incumbent Republicans, holding the other model factors equal. But incumbents in
swing districts that lean towards the other party often
face challengers and sometimes a loss. The 2010 cycle was
particularly hard on incumbent Democrats in the post-2008 Obama win GOP
midterm wave. Two Republicans State Reps that rode that wave to victory
in 2010 face Democratic challengers on November 3 that may be able to
to pull off hard-fought wins.

The four most competitive state legislative races in Massachusetts
feature three GOP incumbents in Democratic-leaning districts with
partisan voter indexes (PVIs) of D+3 to D+9, and incumbent Democrat
Steven Ouellette (D-Westport) in his R+4 8th Bristol district on the
South Coast.

```{r top-four-table}
#| column: page
top_four <- contested |>
    slice_min(abs(dem_margin), n = 4)

# The incumbent/challenger layout assumes every one of the four has an incumbent.
stopifnot(all(top_four$incumbent_status != "No_Incumbent"))

top_four |>
    mutate(dem_is_incumbent = (incumbent_status == "Dem_Incumbent"),
           dem_label = cand_label(dem_candidate_name, "D",
                                  dem_candidate_municipality, FALSE),
           opp_label = cand_label(comparison_candidate_name, opp_pty,
                                  comparison_candidate_municipality, FALSE),
           incumbent = if_else(dem_is_incumbent, dem_label, opp_label),
           challenger = if_else(dem_is_incumbent, opp_label, dem_label),
           incumbent_win_prob = if_else(dem_is_incumbent,
                                        dem_win_prob,
                                        1 - dem_win_prob),
           margin_range = str_c(margin_string(margin_low, opp_pty), " to ",
                                margin_string(margin_high, opp_pty))) |>
    select(district_url, PVI, incumbent, challenger,
           incumbent_win_prob, model, margin_range, district_display) |>
    gt() |>
    gt_theme_538() |>
    fmt_url(columns = district_url, label = from_column("district_display")) |>
    cols_label(district_url = "District",
               incumbent = "Incumbent",
               challenger = "Challenger",
               incumbent_win_prob = "Incumbent win",
               model = "Likely margin",
               margin_range = "75% range") |>
    fmt_percent(columns = "incumbent_win_prob", decimals = 0) |>
    cols_hide(columns = district_display) |>
    cols_align(columns = c("PVI", "incumbent_win_prob", "model",
                           "margin_range"),
               align = "center") |>
    tab_header("The four most competitive legislative races")
```

```{r muni-map-setup}
# Precinct presidential results for 2020 and 2024 on the 2021 district map,
# pinned from mapoli/pvi (commit 68d65052). Split towns are summed only over
# the precincts inside the district.
pct_pres <- read_csv("ma_precincts_districts_pres_2024.csv",
                     show_col_types = FALSE)

pct_geometry <- read_sf("../../_gis/ma_wards_precincts_w_subs.geojson") |>
    select(city_town, State_Rep)

US_Harris_24 <- 75017626
US_Trump_24 <- 77301997
US_Biden_20 <- 81281502
US_Trump_20 <- 74222593

US_PVI_24 <- (US_Harris_24 + US_Biden_20) /
    (US_Harris_24 + US_Trump_24 + US_Biden_20 + US_Trump_20)

district_muni_pvi <- function(district_name) {
    muni_votes <- pct_pres |>
        filter(State_Rep == district_name) |>
        group_by(city_town) |>
        summarize(dem = sum(Harris_24 + Biden_20),
                  gop = sum(Trump_24 + Trump_20)) |>
        mutate(PVI_N = (dem / (dem + gop) - US_PVI_24) * 100,
               PVI = pvi_string(PVI_N),
               label = str_glue("{city_town}\n{PVI}"))
    pct_geometry |>
        filter(State_Rep == district_name) |>
        group_by(city_town) |>
        summarize() |>
        st_simplify(dTolerance = 100) |>
        inner_join(muni_votes, by = "city_town")
}

district_muni_map <- function(district_name) {
    race <- contested |>
        filter(chamber == "House", district == district_name)
    muni_pvi <- district_muni_pvi(district_name)
    tm_shape(muni_pvi) +
        tm_polygons(
            fill = "PVI_N",
            fill.scale = tm_scale_continuous(
                values = margin_palette,
                limits = c(-20, 20),
                midpoint = 0,
                outliers.trunc = c(TRUE, TRUE)
            ),
            fill.legend = tm_legend_hide(),
            fill_alpha = 0.7,
            col = "black",
            lwd = 1,
            id = "city_town",
            popup.vars = c("PVI" = "PVI")
        ) +
        tm_text("label") +
        tm_basemap("OpenStreetMap") +
        tm_title(str_glue("State Representative - {race$district_display} ({race$PVI})"))
}
```

### 9th Norfolk

```{r 9th-norfolk-map, fig.height=6}
district_muni_map("Ninth Norfolk")
```

The tightest race from the model's point of view is between incumbent
State Representative Marcus Vaughn (R-Wrentham) and Democratic
newcomer Thomas Melville (D-Medfield). While the 9th Norfolk district
has a PVI of D+7, it has not been represented by a Democrat since
1993, when Jo Ann Sprague (R-Walpole) led a succession of Republicans
including her successor Scott Brown (R-Wrentham).  Brown went on to
the State Senate and then defeated Martha Coakley (D-Medford) in a
January 2010 special election to replace Edward Kennedy in the
U.S. Senate. Melville is running on a campaign of engagement and
community service and raised almost twice the amount of campign money
raised by incumbent Vaughn ($65,494 to $35,721 in 2026).

### 8th Bristol

```{r 8th-bristol-map, fig.height=6}
district_muni_map("Eighth Bristol")
```

The 8th Bristol State Representative district is a mirror image of the
9th Norfolk in that it has been represented by a Democratic
representative for many years, but has a GOP-leaning PVI rating of
R+4. Steven Ouellette (D-Westport) was elected for the first time in
2024 in a five-way race against Christopher Thrasher (R-Westport) and
three unenrolled candidates including the current GOP nominee Jesse
St. Gelais (R-Acushnet). The South Coast area has seen a great deal of
back-and-forth partisan shifting in the Trump era. Challenger
St. Gelais has raised 20% more money over the past two years and spent
four times more than Ouellette, a notably large spending gap.

### 9th Essex

```{r 9th-essex-map, fig.height=6}
district_muni_map("Ninth Essex")
```

Representative Donald Wong (R-Saugus) has represented the North
Shore's 9th Essex district since 2011, after his 383-vote defeat of
Mark Falzone (D-Saugus) in the 2010 GOP wave election. The 9th Essex
district has a PVI of D+3, giving Lynn dentist and city councilor Pete
Meaney (D-Lynn) a fighting chance in a year when anti-GOP and
anti-incumbent sentiment seems to be high. Meaney was able to
significantly outraise and outspend Wong, which may help to improve
name recognition while competing against the well-known incumbent.

### 3rd Barnstable

```{r 3rd-barnstable-map, fig.height=6}
district_muni_map("Third Barnstable")
```

Incumbent Representative David Vieira (R-Falmouth) also flipped his
House seat from blue to red in the 2010 GOP wave, defeating long-time
incumbent Matthew Patrick (D-Falmouth) to take office in 2011. The D+9
PVI in the 3rd Barnstable district gives Falmouth Select Board member
Jack Richardson (D-Falmouth) a real chance, enhanced by the
fundraising and spending advantage he had over Vieira during the
election cycle.

## Ratings for all contested seats

Our newly revamped Massachusetts legislative election model uses
precinct-level PVI, incumbency status, and fundraising data and is
trained on data from 2010 through 2024. You can look at more details
and do what-if calculations on the
[model website](https://bwbensonjr.github.io/election-modeling/).

Here are the forecast ratings for all of the contested State
Representative and State Senate races.

```{r contested-map, fig.height=6, fig.cap="Contested State Representative and State Senate races. Use the layer control to switch chambers."}
#| column: body-outset
race_layer(house_geom, "House") +
    race_layer(senate_geom, "Senate", show_legend = FALSE) +
    tm_group("House", control = "radio") +
    tm_group("Senate", control = "radio") +
    tm_basemap("OpenStreetMap", group.control = "none") +
    tm_view(set_view = c(-71.6, 42.2, 8))
```

```{r summary-stats}
n_races <- nrow(contested)
n_house <- sum(contested$chamber == "House")
n_senate <- sum(contested$chamber == "Senate")
n_toss <- sum(contested$dem_win_prob > 0.4 & contested$dem_win_prob < 0.6)
n_competitive <- sum(contested$dem_win_prob > 0.095 & contested$dem_win_prob < 0.905)
```

```{r ratings-table}
#| column: screen
contested |>
    arrange(abs(dem_margin)) |>
    mutate(is_top_four = target_id %in% top_four$target_id) |>
    select(chamber, district_url, PVI, Incumbent, Democrat, Opponent,
           model, dem_margin, margin_low, margin_high, is_top_four,
           district_display) |>
    gt() |>
    gt_theme_538() |>
    fmt_url(columns = district_url, label = from_column("district_display")) |>
    cols_label(chamber = "Office",
               district_url = "District",
               model = "Model",
               dem_margin = "Dem margin (75% range)") |>
    gt_plt_conf_int(dem_margin,
                    c(margin_low, margin_high),
                    palette = c("black", "black", "white", "black"),
                    ref_line = 0,
                    text_size = 2.5,
                    width = 55) |>
    cols_hide(columns = c(margin_low, margin_high, is_top_four, district_display)) |>
    cols_align(columns = c("model", "dem_margin"), align = "center") |>
    gt_highlight_rows(font_weight = "normal", rows = is_top_four) |>
    tab_header("Contested 2026 legislative race ratings")
```
